summary: Boer Mountain lookout near Burns Lake: a 1937 radio item calls the station new and a 1985 break-in took its radio; no build date, staffing or current-site record found.

facts.agency: B.C. Forest Service (named in the 1985 item); Forest Branch (named in the 1937 item)

events.note: December 1937 item from the Forest Branch News Letter calls the station 'the new Boer Mountain Lookout Station'. It gives no build date.
Break-in at the B.C. Forest Service lookout on Boer Mountain between April 25 and 27; the station's radio was taken. The page dates the item May 8, 1985.

evidence.supports: Canada Lookouts gives the position and elevation
Page places the lookout in the Bulkley - Nechako area
The 1937 item is quoted from the Forest Branch News Letter
Two-way communication was set up in September 1937 between the Burns Lake ranger station and the new station
evidence.quote: Satisfactory two-way communication was established during September between the Ranger Station at Burns Lake

evidence.supports: The 1985 item is from the Lake District News
1937 item calls the station new and names Asst. Ranger Dick O'Hara
evidence.quote: the new Boer Mountain Lookout Station by Asst. Ranger Dick O'Hara

evidence.supports: Two homemade sets built by Mr. O'Hara were used
evidence.quote: Two homemade sets, built by Mr. O'Hara were used

evidence.supports: Messages came through as clearly as on a city phone
evidence.quote: all messages were received as clearly as on a city phone

evidence.supports: Break-in at the B.C. Forest Service lookout and theft of the station's radio
evidence.quote: Thieves broke into the B.C. Forest Service lookout on Boer Mountain and sometime between April 25 and 27 made off with the station's radio.

evidence.supports: Radio was valued at more than $2,000
evidence.quote: The radio was valued at more than $2,000.

evidence.supports: Police said an investigation was under way
evidence.quote: Police sources said an investigation into the incident was underway.

evidence.supports: Project area of about 155 hectares with bike park, trails and a campground
evidence.quote: The project area of about 155 hectares is home to the Burns Lake Mountain Bike Park and Trails and a small campground.

evidence.supports: The area is heavily used by recreational hikers
evidence.quote: The area is heavily used by recreational hikers

evidence.supports: FESBC lists Burns Lake Community Forest Ltd. as the project organization
evidence.quote: Organization Burns Lake Community Forest Ltd.

evidence.supports: Burns Lake's trail network is on Boer Mountain
evidence.quote: its network of trails on Boer Mountain

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The page dates the 1985 item May 8, 1985 and adds '(one year ago)', which leaves the year open. The story uses the printed 1985 date and says the page gives it.

sources.title: Boer Mountain Wildfire Risk Reduction Treatment

notes_for_editor: Two dated items give the tower a 1937 and 1985 record. Nothing in sources read gives its build date, staffing, fate or present condition. A Facebook group thread (not readable) reportedly carries 1930 and 1939 photos of a Boer Mountain tower and says the build date is unclear; that would sit uneasily with the 1937 'new' station, so it is not used. Lead: the Lakes District Museum Society, whose Facebook post on regional lookouts could not be read. Public access today is only described for the mountain's trails, not the tower.
